headline: PHP2Shell CISA deadline is today; Linux kernel KEV fix due Oct 31; DHS staff leak spreads as Japan's breach wave grows

bullets.text: PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) rooted 25 servers and breached a U.S. government-affiliated network; China-linked actors are rooting firewalls with it. CISA's due date is today, 2026-10-29; fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35.

KEV deadlines: Linux kernel CVE-2026-46300 (missing variable initialization) is due 2026-10-31; Adobe Commerce/Magento CVE-2026-48356 and Google Brotli CVE-2026-111497 are due 2026-11-10; Broadcom VMware ESX CVE-2026-41709 (insufficient logging) is due 2026-11-11.

New: Sony-owned ISP So-net disclosed a breach exposing about 2.5 million customer records, adding to Japan's wave of incidents with GMO (which urged customers to disconnect PCs and offered a $1M bounty) and Japan Airlines.
Personnel data on more than 41,000 DHS employees, including CBP and ICE agents, has been published on a leak site; Bluesky is now blocking links to it.

New: Researchers disclosed a critical 16-year-old UEFI flaw that can run code before Secure Boot on network-booting servers. Adobe also fixed 8 critical Campaign Classic flaws (CVE-2026-104351) allowing code execution.

Still active: Volt Typhoon's 'Silent Train' network hid four zero-day campaigns; attackers are hitting Oracle E-Business Suite RCE CVE-2026-101767 days after the patch; CISA warns Node2Shell is being exploited.

actions: Finish PHP updates to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 today, including firewalls and appliances, and check exposed hosts for compromise.
Apply your distribution's kernel fix for CVE-2026-46300 before 2026-10-31, starting with multi-user and internet-facing Linux hosts.
Patch Adobe Commerce/Magento CVE-2026-48356, Adobe Campaign Classic CVE-2026-104351 and VMware ESX CVE-2026-41709 per vendor advisories.
Review network-booting servers against the UEFI pre-Secure Boot advisory and restrict PXE/network boot to trusted segments.
Apply Oracle's patches for E-Business Suite CVE-2026-101767 and PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273, and check for Node2Shell exposure.
If you work with GMO, So-net or Japan Airlines, follow their notices and watch for phishing using leaked customer data.
